title: Normalization of an ordinary resolution rule on normal inputs
statement:
Fix a smooth-functorial ordinary resolution rule $R$ on all reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, including finite disjoint unions, with the ordered centers and comparison laws of [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]. A scheme is normal here if all its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For a normal input $S$, write $R(S)=(S_n	o\cdots	o S_0=S;I_i)$ and let $
u_i:S_i^
u	o S_i$ be componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Set $N_0=S$, $N_i=S_i^
u$ for $1\leq i\leq n$, and $K_i=I_i\mathcal O_{N_i}$, with $N_0	o S_0$ the identity. Then the induced maps form a finite tower $R^
u(S)$ with
$$N_{i+1}\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{K_i}(N_i)^
u\quad	ext{over }N_i$$
of normalized blowups [def-trf-normalized-blowup]. Every level is normal, reduced and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$; every $K_i$ is coherent, with nonempty nowhere dense zero scheme; and $N_n$ is canonically the regular terminal scheme $S_n$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For $n=0$ this is the trivial tower, and the empty scheme receives the trivial tower.

For every smooth $h:T	o S$ between normal reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the canonical comparisons obtained from those of $R$ and normalization identify $R^
u(T)$ with the contraction of the recursively pulled-back tower $h^*R^
u(S)$. Exactly the stages with unit extended ideal are deleted; at those stages the normalized blowup is an isomorphism. The other centers are exactly the extended $K_i$ in their original order. The level maps and retained-stage indices respect identities and composition, and no stage is deleted when $h$ is surjective.

source.place: Expose VIII, Proposition 2.2.4(ii), 2.2.6, Lemma 2.2.9, 2.3.3(i), 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.12(i), printed pp.90--93; restriction to normal starting schemes makes deletion of unit-ideal stages literal. No single Stacks tag states this tower transformation.

proof.text: First check the hypotheses needed to apply the one-stage calculus to every ordinary level. Inductively each $S_i$ is reduced and finite type over $\mathbf Q$. This holds at $i=0$. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S_i$, take generators $I_i=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$. The cited chart cover identifies the next level locally with $\operatorname{Spec}A[I_i/a_j]$, a subalgebra of $A_{a_j}$ generated by the finitely many fractions $a_k/a_j$. Thus these finitely many charts over a finite affine cover give finite type over $\mathbf Q$. They are reduced: if $(b/a_j^m)^d=0$ in $A_{a_j}$, some $a_j^e b^d=0$; then $(a_j^e b)^d=0$ in the reduced ring $A$, whence $a_j^e b=0$ and $b/a_j^m=0$. A subring of a reduced ring is reduced by the same nilpotence test. Reducedness of the scheme follows from the affine criterion in the cited definition. Empty charts cause no exception.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4, 2.2.6; affine chart verification of reduced finite-type ordinary levels

proof.text: Each $S_i$ is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem, applied over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $1$). Hence each quasi-coherent locally finitely generated $I_i$ of the ordinary rule is coherent by the cited coherence criterion. The zero schemes are nonempty and nowhere dense by the regular-resolution hypothesis in the rule, without any claim that their inverse images under normalization are regular.

source.place: VIII 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.12(ii); coherence on Noetherian ordinary levels

proof.text:
Construct the tower by induction on $i$. At $i=0$, $N_0=S=S^
u$ canonically because $S$ is normal, as in the unit-ideal clause of the normalized-blowup calculus. At a subsequent index the induction identifies $N_i$ with $S_i^
u$. Apply that calculus to $(S_i,I_i)$, whose hypotheses were checked in Steps 1--2. Its comparison over $S_i^
u$ gives
$$S_{i+1}^
u=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i}(S_i)^
u\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i\mathcal O_{N_i}}(N_i)^
u.$$
Use its structural map to $N_i$ as the next transition. This is exactly the normalized blowup in the cited definition; composing the transitions defines all tower maps. The calculus also says that this next level is normal, reduced and finite type over $\mathbf Q$, so the induction starts and continues within the stipulated class. All the maps are over the preceding level, not merely abstract isomorphisms of schemes.

For every $i$, the componentwise-normalization properties say that $\nu_i$ is surjective and takes generic points bijectively to generic points (for $i=0$ it is the identity). The extended-ideal theorem identifies $K_i$ locally with the ideal generated by the images of generators of $I_i$, and says it is quasi-coherent. It is therefore finitely generated locally; $N_i$ is Noetherian by Step 3 and the finite-type theorem, so the coherence criterion makes $K_i$ coherent. Its zero set is $\nu_i^{-1}V(I_i)$: in a local ring map an ideal in the maximal ideal remains in the maximal ideal, and the image of a unit is a unit. Surjectivity makes this zero set nonempty. The generic-point bijection shows it contains no generic point, hence is nowhere dense: a closed subset of a Noetherian scheme has interior only if it contains a generic point of a component. Finally the regular terminal scheme $S_n$ has trivial normalization by the calculus, giving $N_n\simeq S_n$. If $n=0$ the tower is already trivial and $S=S_n$ is regular. On the empty input a nonempty center is impossible, so its ordinary and normalized towers both have length zero.

We will use smoothness after any base change, directly in the stated convention. Local finite presentation is preserved by the cited permanence theorem. For formal smoothness, a map from an affine first-order thickening $D\subset D'$ into the base-changed source gives a map $D\to X$ and a map $D'\to Y'$ over $Y$. Lift $D\to X$ to $D'\to X$ by formal smoothness of $X\to Y$; pair that lift with $D'\to Y'$ using the fibre-product property. This is the required lift to $X\times_Y Y'$. The smoothness definition therefore applies, with no assumption on $Y'\to Y$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 2.2.9, smooth specialization; direct lifting check and local finite presentation permanence

proof.text:
Let $R(T)$ have ordinary levels $T_j$, and let $r,c$ and $g_i:T_{c(i)}\to S_i$ be the contracted comparison of the ordinary rule for $h$. Each $g_i$ is a base change of $h$, hence smooth by Step 5. Put $M_0=T$ and $M_j=T_j^\nu$ for $j>0$. The normalization comparison in the calculus, applied to $g_i$ (using its unit-ideal case if needed), gives
$$M_{c(i)}\simeq S_i^\nu\times_{S_i}T_{c(i)}\simeq N_i\times_S T.$$
When $c(i)=0$ use the assumed normality of $T$; at $i=0$ use normality of $S$. The second isomorphism uses the cartesian square supplied by the ordinary comparison. At a retained stage $i=r(k)$ the ideal on $T_k$ is $I_i\mathcal O_{T_k}$ by that comparison. Extending to $M_k$ gives $(I_i\mathcal O_{T_k})\mathcal O_{M_k}=K_i\mathcal O_{M_k}$: both are locally generated by the same images of sections of $I_i$, by the extended-ideal theorem. The smooth normalized-blowup comparison in the calculus identifies the next structural map with the recursively pulled-back normalized blowup. Induction on $i$, starting with $M_0=T$, now gives the required comparison at every level, including the maps to the preceding levels.

source.place: VIII 2.2.6--2.2.9, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.12(i): levelwise normalization of the ordinary comparisons

proof.text: At an omitted ordinary stage the ideal on $T_{c(i)}$ is unit, so its extension to $M_{c(i)}$ is unit. Conversely a nonunit ideal there stays nonunit after normalization: choose a point in its zero scheme, lift it by surjectivity of $M_{c(i)}\to T_{c(i)}$, and use the local-ring observation of Step 4. Thus the ordinary and normalized comparisons have exactly the same omitted indices. At an omitted normalized stage the current level is normal by Step 3 (applied also to $T$), and the calculus says its unit-ideal normalized blowup is the identity. Deleting it is therefore legitimate; all other ideals remain in the order specified by $r$. For the empty source every ideal extends to the unique unit ideal and all stages disappear. No assertion is made that every isomorphism stage must disappear: a nonunit Cartier ideal can have an isomorphic blowup and remains a retained center.

source.place: VIII 2.3.4--2.3.5(i) and Remark 2.3.12(i); unit-stage contraction on normal inputs

proof.text: For the identity, the ordinary comparison has identity counts, indices and maps; the normalized comparisons are identities by the calculus. For $U\xrightarrow{a}T\xrightarrow{h}S$, the ordinary counts compose as $c_{ha}=c_a\circ c_h$ and the retained embeddings compose as $r_{ha}=r_h\circ r_a$, with the stipulated transports. Step 7 shows that normalization uses exactly these same indices. On each retained transition the calculus says its base-change comparison respects composition; the ideal equalities are successive extensions of the same sections. Induction on the ordered indices therefore gives the equality of the level maps for $ha$ and the composite comparisons. Deleted transitions are identities, so they do not alter this equality. If $h$ is surjective, the ordinary retained embedding is surjective by the rule; the identical retained embedding for the normalized tower deletes no stage. This proves all the comparison laws.

source.place: VIII 2.3.4--2.3.5(i), Remark 2.3.12(i); identity and composite comparison laws

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII, Proposition 2.2.4(ii), 2.2.6--2.2.9, Remark 2.3.3(i), 2.3.4--2.3.5(i) and Remark 2.3.12(i), printed pp.90--93; explicit finite induction and ideal checks
